readerReview: Full 35-section map and complete prior 20-line film; complete sources 1,4,5,7,8,13,21,23,30,31,34 read. This includes the opening definition and its limits, state/monetary history, protocol society, institutional intelligence, epilogue and scope note. Source8 contains a damaged table extraction; no claims rely on reconstructed table data. This is selected source reading, not the complete 241k-character book or external bibliography verification.

figures.decision: Inspected; not directly embedded. Cover and dense static source figures are reserved for reading; original conceptual staging preserves the relevant relation without presenting model values as measurements.

artMeaning: An inhabited quay has a ship, physically supported cargo, hoist and workers. An actual cargo contract is examined before release, making the book’s material/social relationship visible. No decorative yin-yang icon, invented historical port or automatic release outcome.

A seller first retains a parcel despite a physically present coin. The same marked coin is compared to a recognized unit, followed by explicit seller acceptance and a settlement entry; only then do coin, parcel and receipt change hands. An issuing office reveals dependence on recognized authority. This is a labeled illustrative transaction, not a coin-origin story or a magic stamp guarantee.

A persistent official ledger survives clerk turnover. The merchant’s receipt bears the same parcel and accepted-payment mark, while the ledger lacks that entry. The mismatch can be examined and taken to an outside reviewer; storage and correction are visibly different operations. No automatic correction, debt cancellation or legal victory is invented.

A contemporary terminal repeats the old missing-payment entry, while the user still holds contradictory evidence. A separate human reviewer receives the receipt and the governing rule; the proposed revision remains pending. The closing physical book offers The Double Technology of Civilization and Protocol Society as the reading route. No instant appeal win, legal instruction or AI inevitability.
epistemicLimits: The port and repeated payment are hypothetical explanatory scenes, not historical evidence or a real currency.
The coin remains physically identical before and after recognition; recognized denomination and an accepted settlement process jointly matter, not a magic stamp.
The receipt/ledger disagreement illustrates the source’s institutional correction problem, not a claimed documented banking event.
People interpret and contest rules; the book does not equate people with mechanical components.
A review route does not guarantee a correct decision, payment recovery, legal entitlement or institutional legitimacy.
AI effects and future safeguards remain proposed and contingent; no world-first, inevitable progress, universal history ladder or guaranteed decentralized outcome.
figureReview: Only source image is the cover, inspected. The yin-yang graphic communicates the book’s paired technology metaphor but offers no empirical diagram; the new original dock/transaction/record/terminal art enacts the relationship instead of using an ornamental symbol.
